works.author: hoan-ton-that
works.title: Statement of Hoan Ton-That before the Massachusetts Special Commission on Facial Recognition

statements.where: 'Any ban on facial recognition will be devastating...' paragraph, p.2

works.note: Argues law enforcement should keep using facial recognition over a 3-billion-image web-scraped database to fight crime; opposes bans and DMV/mugshot-only limits. PDF text extracts cleanly.

works.author: palmer-luckey
works.title: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III (TED)

statements.where: passage quoting the objection 'You should never allow AI to decide who lives and who dies' and answering 'no moral high ground in saying, I refuse to use AI'

works.note: Single-speaker talk; transcript is auto-generated from captions. Alternative source: CBS 60 Minutes transcript (cbsnews.com/news/palmer-luckey-ai-powered-autonomous-weapons-future-of-warfare-60-minutes-transcript), where he describes weapons that 'identify, select, and engage targets... No operator needed'.

works.author: scott-alexander
works.title: The Pentagon Threatens Anthropic

statements.where: 'AI-enabled mass surveillance of US citizens seems like the sort of thing we should at least have a chance to think over'
'we'll probably get them eventually'; calls himself 'a sensible moderate on the killbot issue'

works.note: Soft on both: surveillance line is a call for deliberation, not an outright bar; killbot line accepts eventual autonomous weapons rather than arguing for them.

works.author: dean-ball
works.title: Clawed: On Anthropic and the Department of War

statements.where: 'mass surveillance and autonomous weapons/systems of control cannot be used to curtail our liberties'; 'You can support restrictions on mass domestic surveillance...'

works.note: Ball supports restrictions on mass domestic surveillance by law but objects to imposing them via a private defense contract. Adds a hold-side figure (statement had only 3 total).

works.author: brian-merchant
works.title: How to kick Flock out of your town

statements.where: intro framing: 'Abuse of the system has been rampant'; 'the burgeoning movement to defang the surveillance state'

works.note: Intro co-written with Ryan Hodes, followed by an interview with a DeFlock organizer; only Merchant's framing counts. About AI plate-reader networks used by police to track movements.

works.author: gary-marcus
works.title: Has Google gone too woke? Why even the biggest models still struggle with guardrails

statements.where: 'not however intended as an anti-woke screed'; 'I think it is just lousy software'

works.note: Attributes Gemini's image controversy to technical guardrail failure, not political bias; rejects the 'anti-white' partisan framing.

works.author: scott-alexander
works.title: AI Safety Is Not A Corporate Plot

statements.where: 'The experts are warning you that AI could kill you because they think AI could kill you'; 'all these people believed it then, and still believe it now'

works.note: Argues AI-lab leaders' risk warnings are sincere, not hype. Caveat for readers: includes a jab that Altman's 2015 warning was 'the one time in his life' he was fully honest, so it is about sincerity of risk warnings, not general candour.

works.author: alex-tabarrok
works.title: What Regulatory Capture Actually Looks Like

statements.where: 'We also have plenty of evidence that the fears of AI experts are sincere'; closing 'Amodei actually believes what he's saying'

works.note: Rebuts the claim that AI-risk talk is a regulatory-capture ploy; notes Amodei, Altman and Musk warned before they had companies.

works.author: brian-merchant
works.title: This Labor Day, let's consider how we want technology to work for us

statements.where: 'a relatively few technology owners might benefit'; closing hope for technology 'democratically developed, worker-first, and wielded for the public good'

works.note: Argues owner-directed automation degrades jobs; calls for shifting decision power over tech to labor.

works.author: ed-zitron
works.title: The Rot Economy

statements.where: Google Search section: 'a source of information corrupted by a profit-seeking entity'; Facebook/Instagram 'endlessly profitable and utterly useless'

works.note: Core thesis: growth-at-all-costs incentives make tech products worse for users.

works.author: garett-jones
works.title: Garett Jones: Immigration, national IQ, & less democracy (Dwarkesh Podcast)

works.note: Speaker-labelled transcript. Argues for shifting authority to appointed experts (FDA/CDC 'more like the Fed').
